duration_model.expr: (fadestart + fadedur) if (fadestart + fadedur) < indur else indur

description: Fades the sound to zero starting at fadestart, over fadedur - and TRUNCATES the file where the fade completes: output duration = fadestart + fadedur (clipped to the input duration when the fade would overrun - verified: 1.5+1.5 on a 2 s file yields 2.0). Model exact at both probed input durations (1.0+0.5 -> 1.5000 from 2 s; 0.3+0.4 -> 0.7000 from 1 s). Mode 2 of 6 (fade start + DURATION - the most composable form; mode 1 takes start+end times, mode 3 fades to the existing file end; modes 4-6 are the same three with a fixed doubly-exponential slope). envtype 0 = linear, 1 = exponential (default); the binary also accepts the family's undocumented 2 ('steep') and 3 ('doubly exponential') - and mode 1 with envtype 3 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to mode 4, mode 3 with envtype 3 to mode 6, so the steep modes need no separate entries. All params refuse breakpoints. Deterministic; stereo accepted.
musical_use: Fade-out plus cut in one deterministic move: end a phrase exactly where you want it with a musical die-away instead of a hard edit. Because the output length is fadestart+fadedur by construction, it slots directly into duration arithmetic - trim iteration tails, shape loop segments to exact lengths, or mass-produce decaying fragments whose total lengths you control. Exponential (1) reads as natural decay; linear (0) keeps low-level content audible to the very end; the undocumented 3 gives the steepest, most 'gated-reverb' cutoff. Complementary tools: envel dovetail fades both edges in place (no truncation), sfedit cut takes a region without fading, envnu expdecay imposes an exponential decay whose endpoint also truncates.

fadestart.description: Time the fade begins (seconds by default; samples or grouped-samples via the times flag). Out-of-bounds values refuse at runtime with 'ERROR: Start of fade time : out of range.' (not a Parameter[N] message). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1'). Scalar only.

fadedur.description: Duration of the fade-out; the file ends when it completes (fadestart + fadedur), clipped to the input duration. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2'). Scalar only.

envtype.description: Fade shape: 0 linear, 1 exponential (documented default). UNDOCUMENTED 2 ('steep') and 3 ('doubly exponential') are accepted - the dovetail-family ENVTYPE enum; envtype 3 reproduces the mode 4-6 slope exactly (byte-verified). Values above 3 die with 'ERROR: Unknown case in create_envelope()' (internal error, not a range message). Scalar only.

times.description: Unit of fadestart/fadedur: 0 seconds (default when omitted), 1 samples, 2 grouped-samples - same convention as envel dovetail. Scalar only.

examples.description: End a phrase at exactly 1.5 s with a natural die-away.
examples.expected_use: Output is exactly 1.5 s: untouched to 1.0 s, exponential fade to zero across the last 0.5 s.

examples.description: Steepest cutoff (the 'mode 5' slope without the broken mode).
examples.expected_use: Doubly-exponential clamp - byte-equivalent to the mode 4-6 slope family; see known_issues for why mode 5 itself is unusable.

known_issues: BINARY BUG - MODE 5 IS BROKEN on this build: 'envel curtail 5' (fadestart + fadedur, doubly-exponential) dies every time with 'ERROR: INSUFFICIENT MEMORY to reallocate level array.' while modes 4 and 6 work. This entry with envtype 3 reproduces exactly what mode 5 should do (mode-equivalence byte-verified on the 1<->4 and 3<->6 pairs).

Duration model verified exact at two input durations plus the overrun-clip case (fadestart+fadedur > indur returns the full input, fade compressed to what remains... verified output 2.0000 from 1.5+1.5 on 2 s).
envtype > 3 aborts with an internal error ('Unknown case in create_envelope()'), not a range refusal - the schema max of 3 is the curator's pin of the source enum.
Sibling modes: 1 (start+end times, model = fadeend), 3 (start only, static duration), 4/6 (= 1/3 at envtype 3, byte-verified) - all reachable via execute(); only mode 2 is curated.
All params scalar-only (breakpoints refused, parameters 1-2 verbatim). Deterministic; stereo accepted.
